reviews.title: A young 69
reviews.text: People tell me I am a young 69, and I attribute much of that to doing TRX. A lot of times what I’m doing may not match what I’m watching - doesn’t keep me from doing it anyway! Go Louis!

reviews.title: In app pricing is deceptive
reviews.text: Your in app pricing on the App Store is grossly out of date or deceptive. App Store shows $39.99 for yearly subscription. App itself lists $199! What gives?

reviews.title: 6 years
reviews.text: I bought the TRX about six years ago, installed it into the trusses in my basement. I’m almost 50 years old, and in some of the best shape that I’ve ever been even after being a college athlete.  Can’t say enough about it.

reviews.title: Workouts not playing

reviews.title: La mejor app
reviews.text: He probado muchas app para ejercitarme y TRX realmente a sido la más completa que encontrado. Soy Salvavidas y nadadora, me encanta que tiene una sección de ejercicios solo para nadadores, me encanta mucho.

reviews.title: No search bar?  Filtering is poor
reviews.text: Lacks a search.  A basic search to weed through 100s of videos.  Oh, and I guess that swimming is not a sport even though you have swimming workouts!   Lastly, the auto rotation detection is weak… gotta hit the rotate icon.   So far I’m not impressed enough to pay the monthly fee

reviews.title: Buggy
reviews.text: This app is so buggy. Perfect Wi-Fi and the videos still freeze constantly. Such an interruption to the workout. If you want to use their ply music feature—good luck. The freezing gets worse.

reviews.title: Awesome Keith!
reviews.text: Great workout with Keith. His instructions are clear and he gives options for different fitness levels. Really “enjoyed” his workout.  “Enjoyed” may be an over exaggeration 😜

reviews.title: Great looking app not for me.
reviews.text: The app is very well put together with excellent time-based training.  It just doesn’t work for me. I’m new to suspension training, and I would like more guidance on how to perform the exercises correctly in the app, including the angles and levers, and when to choose one exercise over another.  It would be nice to be able to use a library of exercises without having to subscribe, even on a limited basis, for a simple understanding of correct form and what to avoid. It would be helpful to be able to build your own routine to achieve personalized fitness goals.  Trying to learn the correct setup for time-based workouts is difficult; there’s no single set for how to do the basic exercises without a subscription, so you have to jump to YouTube or the desktop website.

reviews.title: The optimal system
reviews.text: There aren’t many systems for resistance training that can accommodate essentially anyone, anywhere. TRX is the ultimate home and travel workout system. I’ve been a competitive bodybuilder and as I’ve gotten older and dealing with some injuries and pain issues, TRX still offers a complete and challenging workout without being tied to a gym or risking injury from lifting barbells and dumbbells

reviews.title: Great variety
reviews.text: Really great variety of workouts to choose from

reviews.title: No basic value
reviews.text: Love the TRX, but this app lacks basic value. To start it forces you to register to then ask you to subscribe. That is a way to collect data before showing your value. Then, it doesn’t provide a list of exercises you can do with the TRX outside of a routine, for which you guess, you have to pay for. That is basic. Why do I need to use a third party app to use your product? Offering custom workouts or tracking progress grants a subscription, but showing a list of what can be done with a TRX does not. That is disappointing.

reviews.title: Stronger in 12
reviews.text: First time doing TRX on my own. I can feel the burn.  Hopefully I get better adjusting the TRX strap.  It is a little confusing.

reviews.title: Good Content, Poorly Designed App
reviews.text: Lots of good content.  Unfortunately it’s hidden in a buggy app prone to freezing.  Support while responsive is unhelpful (Really the best you can do is reinstall, sign out and   sign in again).  Searching is non existent, although, you can set up very basic and limited filters.  For what you get the subscription fee is expensive.   Luckily most of the content is available elsewhere for free!

reviews.title: Trash
reviews.text: This app is awful. I can’t get any of the videos to play and it takes forever to load. It’s extremely buggy and I regret purchasing this whole system.

reviews.title: Golf Workout
reviews.text: TR talks WAY TOO MUCH.

reviews.title: No Search for Workouts
reviews.text:
Love the gear. I wanted to love the app, but the filter for finding workouts is limited and requires pages of scrolling to find what you want. 

I saw an “over 50” workout I wanted to try and figured I could search for it later. Nope. There is no “over 50” filter. The available filters returned pages of unrelated workouts. 

I suspect the experience is the same for anyone searching for any specific workout—pages of generally related workouts, but not the specific one they are looking for. 

Good app UIs aren’t hard. The best practices are out there. 

Please, TRX, give us proper search in the app. In the meantime I’m cancelling my subscription and using free videos on YouTube.

reviews.title: TRX Straps
reviews.text: Have them now for about 5 years, great quality and they hold up well. Great for training on the go or for a good warm up before you hit some weights. Makes working out a lot more fun!

reviews.title: Getting better
reviews.text: Appreciate the recent navigational changes— far more straightforward. Mostly easy to use but one request! When playing a video, I wish the video controls would auto hide. As it is now, when I hit pause and then unpause I have to tap again to hide the play overlay so I can see the video clearly.  I always forget, dive back into my workout and then have to return to the iPad to tap it, which is annoying. Most other playback apps auto hide the controls after a few secs.

reviews.title: 2nd vote for a shady company

My account even says that I do not have a subscription but they keep charging me. The other shady thing is that my information in my login page does not even show my credit card that I have on file so I can delete it. I consider this a crime and they are stealing from me. I plan to post every time they charge me.

reviews.title: Great app
reviews.text: Tons of various routines.  Love the different levels of intensity. Never get bored. Only difficulty is picking which work out to do.

reviews.title: Go-to workout for years now
reviews.text:
We first got a TRX set and subscription during Covid so that we could work out from home. I got into the routine of doing 30 minutes of advanced workout every day. It’s by far the best workout I’ve ever had. I know I have access to a full gym, but I still almost always just use the TRX straps and the on demand workouts. 

You can do full body work out to give you the same level of cardio you can get on a run.

reviews.title: Better than expected
reviews.text:
Every time I workout, I’m amazed at what a great workout I get with minimal equipment. It proves that one piece of relatively inexpensive equipment, along with quality instruction, is all you need to get a great workout. 
Additionally, I love the instructors and the range of challenging workouts that are offered on the platform.

reviews.title: All I need

reviews.title: Workout go to

You can always learn new things.  Progress at your own pace . Challenge yourself one day and the next day take it easy and let your body focus on recovery . All in one app.  Keep it up guys.

reviews.title: Shady company
reviews.text: I was automatically enrolled in a monthly subscription when I first purchased my TRX system and created an account in September 2024. I forgot to cancel the plan before the free trial ended, but I cancelled it immediately after seeing the first charge hit my credit card. Thinking it was done, I didn’t notice until a few months later that I was still being charged each month. I confirmed that the monthly plan was cancelled in my app and reached out to my credit card company to dispute the charge and make sure any pending subscription was cancelled. Again thinking it was settled, I didn’t notice until yesterday that I was still be charged monthly. I reached out to TRX, and they suggested waiving their “policy” by offering me a 3 month refund. They could see in the system when I cancelled my plan, but they refused to acknowledge their mistake in continuing to fraudulently charge me. They subsequently only gave me a refund for June rather than for 3 months much less the 6 other unauthorized monthly charges they placed on my account. While the TRX system is quality, the company is not. If you make the mistake of signing up for a trial with them, make sure you’re more proactive than I was about disputing unauthorized charges, because you’ll probably never see the money again if you’re not vigilant.

reviews.text: I have specific things I want to do on TRX but can’t search these things because the app has no search feature. I can find them for free on YouTube so paying a subscription for this is a waste.

reviews.title: Charged hundred of dollars without an option to cancel
reviews.text: Scam vendor, avoid at all costs. Doesn't matter if you cancel, they still keep charging you!

reviews.title: Videos Great, App awful
reviews.text: The video content is great and I love that part. It’s very much let down my the quality of the app itself. The inability to download workouts for travel (to remote places where TRX is marketed as one of its selling points) is a deal breaker. Saving workouts is clunky, and you cannot save a ‘program,’ but instead have to save an individual workout. So every time I want to go back to the program I’m on, I have to browse and find it in the app. The app is also very slow to load (on new iPad running latest iOS and fast WiFi), and crashes often. Please fix these issues and make it to the same standard as the content.

reviews.title: High cost, low value
reviews.text: For how much money a subscription costs, you’d think the app would work with devices like apple watch (which they advertise, but does NOT work), and that the user experience in the app would be nice. Instead, the app is pretty clunky, workouts are led by amateurs who mix up cues, and it doesn’t even integrate properly with health apps. You’re better off seeking out fitness apps from other providers.

reviews.title: iPad app crashes after latest update
reviews.text: The TRX app for iPad constantly crashes after the September update. When one hits the button to activate a live class the app turns off. I see no problems with the iPhone app however. Please fix.
